newsitem.title: INDIA: Low gold prices to fuel India sub-continent demand.
newsitem.headline: Low gold prices to fuel India sub-continent demand.

text.p: Falling world gold prices and a liberalised import policy are expected to boost demand in India while increased jewellery-buying during Ramadan may push it up in Pakistan in the near term, dealers said on Monday.
"Indian demand for gold will certainly get a boost from falling world prices," said Makhan Lal Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Association.
Damani said he would expect global gold prices to fall further from Friday's three-year low of $364.30 per ounce but would not hazard a guess.
"The global trend will bring down Indian prices but will boost the demand," he said. "The fall in prices also coincides with renewed wedding demand from mid-January."
On the Bombay bullion market gold prices fell by 125 rupees to 4,950 rupees per 10 grams in the week to Monday and dealers said they expected it to fall further this week.

"If global prices continue to remain depressed, India's gold imports can easily exceed 500 tonnes in 1997," Damani said. India, the largest consumer of gold, used about 500 tonnes in 1996, according to trade estimates.
Bullion analyst Madhusudan Daga said a measure India announced last week to liberalise its gold import policy would help improve supplies, coming at a time when world prices were low.
On December 31 India said it would allow expatriate Indians to bring in 10 kgs (22 lbs) of gold, subject to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grams, once every six months, instead of five kgs at present.
"Imports of gold will certainly go up," said Daga, adding that it would also stem smuggling of the metal to some extent.
Last month India's revenue officials seized 62 kgs (140.8 lbs) of smuggled gold, their biggest haul of the contraband metal since India allowed official imports of gold in 1992.
In Hong Kong, gold prices closed at $360.50/361.00 per ounce on Monday against New York's closing of $360.75/361.25 and some traders forecast it would touch $350 within a month.
Dealers in Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi said they would expect gold prices to rise further on higher demand in the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, beginning next week.
They said the Eid-ul-Fitr religious feast and the March-April wedding season could aid demand and prices, which in the week to Sunday fell 153 rupees per 10 grams to 5,110 rupees.

Dealers in Dubai, the hub of Gulf trading, said bullion sales to the Indian subcontinent remained dull despite low global prices and anticipated wedding demand in India and liberalised import of gold into this country.
"Business has not been as good as I had hoped...Buying is not as strong as last year," said one Dubai-based trader.
Traders said the relaxation of Indian laws governing the import of gold would help push up exports from Dubai to India.
"It should attract more (bullion) carriers (to India)," one wholesaler said.
